final_candidates.decision_summary: Located in the Sa antigenic loop, this charge-reversal mutation disrupts key neutralizing antibody epitopes while preserving overall hemagglutinin folding and replication fitness.
Situated in the Sb antigenic site near the receptor-binding margin, K187E confers broad escape from Sb-directed monoclonal antibodies while maintaining functional cell entry.
A well-characterized Sa site mutation that introduces steric hindrance against neutralizing antibodies without compromising viral fitness.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool is optimized across major neutralizing sites (Sa and Sb) and further unassisted self-iteration is unlikely to improve candidate selection.

history.rationale: Located in the Sa antigenic loop, K176 is a primary contact residue for head-directed neutralizing antibodies where charge reversal confers strong escape. Deep mutational scanning confirms that acidic substitutions at this position maintain robust viral replication fitness.
K176E sits prominently on the Sa antigenic loop and charge reversal strongly disrupts neutralizing antibodies while well tolerated for viral replication.

Position 158 resides within the Sa antigenic site and frequently mediates antibody escape in circulating and experimental H1 strains. The S158N substitution alters epitope topography while remaining well tolerated for viral packaging and entry.
S158N is a well-characterized escape mutation in the Sa site that retains high fitness across H1N1 backgrounds.

K170 lies at the apex of the Sa antigenic site, where substitution to glutamate disrupts electrostatic contacts with monoclonal antibodies. The head domain readily accommodates this change without destabilizing the hemagglutinin trimer.
K170E alters the loop adjacent to the Sa site, providing escape from Sa-directed antibodies with minimal impact on trimer stability.

K187 is situated in the Sb antigenic region adjacent to the receptor-binding domain. Charge substitution provides substantial escape from Sb-targeting antibodies while preserving sialic acid receptor binding competence.
K187E is located in the key Sb antigenic site near the receptor binding margin, conferring broad monoclonal antibody escape without impairing cell entry.

S173 is an exposed Sa site residue where asparagine introduces steric alterations that impair antibody recognition. This substitution is naturally prevalent in evolutionary escape variants and retains high replication capacity.
S173N introduces steric alteration on the surface-exposed Sa loop while maintaining viral infectivity.
Position 185 is within the antigenic site Sb near the 190-helix. Mutating lysine to threonine eliminates key antibody interactions while maintaining functional trimer stability.
K185T targets the Sb site loop, weakening antibody binding while preserving local backbone conformation.
G171 sits in the flexible tip of the Sa antigenic loop. Introducing glutamate creates local charge repulsion against neutralizing immunoglobulins while preserving loop backbone flexibility.
G171E introduces a bulky charged side chain at the apex loop that sterically hinders antibody paratopes.
N179 is located on the solvent-exposed face of the Sa loop. Aspartate substitution alters surface electrostatics to evade neutralizing sera without impacting HA folding.
N179D provides electrostatic variation on the Sa fringe with mild functional fitness impact.

R162 flanks the Sa antigenic region and participates in antibody recognition. A conservative lysine substitution subtly reshapes the local epitope geometry to reduce binding affinity while fully preserving fitness.
R162K is a conservative change at antigenic site Sa conferring modest escape from specific polyclonal sera.
R224 is an exposed residue within the Ca antigenic site. Neutralization of the positive charge attenuates Ca-specific antibody binding without compromising cell surface fusion machinery.
R224Q targets the Ca2 antigenic region, though proximity to the receptor binding pocket carries slight fitness risk.
